title: Top 5 Photography Studios for Rent in Melbourne
summary: Compare the 5 top Melbourne photography studios for rent. Pricing from $45/hr, cycloramas, natural lighting, and pro equipment included.
body_text: Key Takeaways Melbourne has over 30 professional photography studios available for rent, with hourly rates starting around $45 and averaging $120 across the city. Top-rated spaces include SUNSTUDIOS Melbourne (three premium studios with cycloramas in South Melbourne), Bohemia Bay Studio (self-access from $109/hr in Bayside), and K-Studio (six themed photography zones from $119/hr in South Melbourne). Most Melbourne studios include lighting equipment, backdrops, and basic amenities in the hire price, and many are open seven days a week. Studios closer to the CBD tend to cost more ( $163/hr on average) than those in surrounding suburbs. Whether you're planning a fashion editorial, product shoot, or portfolio session, finding the right photography studio rental in Melbourne can shape the outcome of your final images. Melbourne's creative scene is thriving, and there are more photography spaces for rent across the city than ever before. ‍ This guide covers current pricing, verified amenities, and a range of studio picks to help you find the best studio space for your next shoot. From premium facilities backed by Canon to budget-friendly warehouse conversions open seven days a week, here are five of Melbourne's best photo studios for hire. Melbourne Photography Studios at a Glance Studio Location Size From Best For SUNSTUDIOS South Melbourne 3 studios Contact Commercial, fashion Bohemia Bay Cheltenham 160 m² $109/hr Portraits, content creation K-Studio South Melbourne 140 m² $119/hr Portrait, fashion, lifestyle XO Studios Brunswick East 330 m² Contact Product, e-commerce, set builds Lithium Studios Thornbury 8×8m cyc Contact Video, tech-forward photo 1. SUNSTUDIOS Melbourne SUNSTUDIOS Melbourne is one of the most established photography studios in Australia, backed by Canon and housed in a purpose-built facility on Buckhurst Street. The South Melbourne space offers three recently renovated studios, each equipped with a full cyclorama, black curtains, and a Bose sound system. ‍ The facility goes well beyond the basics. Every studio includes private green rooms, hair and makeup stations, clothing racks, digi-op tables, and product tables. On-site amenities include a barista, dedicated roller-door access for seamless load-in, and ample parking. The equipment hire department is just steps away, so that you can add lighting equipment, camera bodies, or lenses to your booking without planning days in advance. ‍ SUNSTUDIOS sits 10 to 25 minutes from Melbourne CBD and 30 minutes from the airport. It's a premium option with pricing to match, but for commercial shoots where equipment quality and reliability are non-negotiable, it's hard to beat. 2. Bohemia Bay Studio Bohemia Bay Studio is a 160-square-meter warehouse in Bayside Melbourne that operates as a fully self-accessible photography studio. There's no studio manager on-site; just you, your crew, and complete creative control. The space offers availability 365 days a year from 7 am to midnight, making it one of the most flexible photography spaces for rent in Melbourne. ‍ The hire fee covers all lighting equipment (strobes, continuous LEDs, and modifiers), a full grip package with C-stands and sandbags, multiple backdrops, a makeup station, dressing area, WiFi, refreshments, and parking. Half-day bookings (4 hours) are $349, and a full day (8 hours) costs $649. ‍ With 49 five-star reviews and a FlexiBook guarantee, Bohemia Bay has built a strong reputation for reliability and value. If you need a well-equipped studio space without CBD pricing, this is a solid option. 3. K-Studio K-Studio occupies 140 square meters on Buckhurst Street in South Melbourne and stands out for its six professionally styled photography zones. Each zone delivers a distinct look: an artificial plant wall, a dark blue accent wall, a bed setup with natural light window, a grand piano with a crystal chandelier and black walls, a Chesterfield sofa with a black velvet curtain, and a 3.5-by-5-meter cyclorama. ‍ This variety means you can produce multiple looks in a single booking without hauling your own props or backdrops. Professional lighting and essential studio gear are included in the rental. The space also offers a fully equipped kitchen with a coffee machine, refrigerator, and microwave, plus a relaxation area for breaks between setups. ‍ Pricing scales with duration: two hours cost $209, a half day (4 hours) runs $349, and a full day (8 hours) is $649. Cancellations made seven or more days in advance receive a full refund; within seven days, down to 24 hours in advance, a 50% refund applies. After-hours sessions are available on request. 4. XO Studios XO Studios is one of Melbourne's larger photography spaces for rent, with Studio 1 offering 330 square meters of light-filled warehouse space in Brunswick East. The facility includes a large cyclorama studio and a smaller secondary studio with a kitchen setup, giving you multiple shooting options under one roof. ‍ The warehouse format provides drive-in access for easy load-in of props, furniture, or vehicles, along with free all-day parking nearby. Natural lighting is abundant, and the open floor plan accommodates large set builds and crew sizes that smaller studios can't support. XO sits about 15 minutes from Melbourne CBD and 20 minutes from the airport. ‍ XO Studios also provides in-house product photography and e-commerce services for businesses that prefer a fully managed shoot rather than a DIY studio hire. 5. Lithium Studios Lithium Studios in Thornbury takes a technology-driven approach to studio hire. The standout feature is an 8-by-8-meter corner cyclorama paired with a 5-by-5-meter overhead lighting grid fitted with four Aperture Nova P300C LED panels and softboxes. This setup delivers soft, controllable top-down lighting without the time-consuming setup required by traditional strobe and modifier rigs. ‍ The space serves both photographers and filmmakers, with curated living and kitchen areas that double as shooting sets or breakout spaces for client meetings between takes. Lithium sits just seven kilometers north-east of Melbourne CBD and is available seven days a week with flexible start and finish times. ‍ For photographers who want advanced lighting equipment already rigged and ready to go, Lithium Studios removes significant setup time from every shoot. ‍ How to Choose the Right Photography Studio in Melbourne Finding the right studio space depends on what you're shooting, how much gear you need, and how long you'll be there. Here are the main factors to weigh. Size and Layout Melbourne studios range from 130 to over 330 square meters. A headshot or portrait session works fine in a smaller space, but product shoots with multiple setups, fashion editorials with large styling teams, or any shoot involving set builds will benefit from more room. Check ceiling height too, especially if you're working with overhead lighting rigs or shooting tall subjects. Lighting Some studios prioritize natural lighting from large windows, while others offer fully blacked-out spaces with professional strobe and LED equipment included. Studios with built-in lighting grids, like Lithium Studios, save considerable setup time. Studios with large windows and natural light work best for organic, lifestyle aesthetics. Equipment Included Most Melbourne photo studios include basic lighting equipment and backdrops in the hire price. Some go further with grip packages, modifiers, and specialty gear. If your project requires a green screen for compositing work, ask about availability, as some studios offer them as add-on rentals. Check what's included before booking separate equipment hire; the all-inclusive cost might be lower at a slightly pricier studio. Cyclorama If you need seamless white or colored backgrounds, look for a studio with a built-in cyclorama. Sizes vary significantly. Lithium Studios offers an 8-meter corner cyc, SUNSTUDIOS has full cycloramas in all three studios, and K-Studio provides a 3.5-by-5-meter cyc that works well for individual portraits but won't accommodate wide compositions. Location and Access Studios in South Melbourne and Fitzroy tend to be closest to the CBD. If you're transporting heavy equipment or props, check for drive-in access and dedicated parking. Studios like XO Studios and Bohemia Bay Studio offer both. Hours and Flexibility Operating hours vary. Bohemia Bay runs from 7 am to midnight year-round, while K-Studio operates from 8 am to 8 pm, with after-hours availability on request. If your shoot schedule is unpredictable, flexibility should factor into your decision. Photography Studio Rental Rates in Melbourne Photography studio rental rates in Melbourne vary based on location, size, and included equipment. ‍ Most studios offer lower per-hour rates for longer bookings. A full day at Bohemia Bay Studio costs $649 for 8 hours (roughly $81/hr), compared to $109/hr for a single-hour booking. K-Studio follows a similar pattern, dropping from $119/hr to about $81/hr for a full day. ‍ Premium studios like SUNSTUDIOS Melbourne price on a project basis and sit above the market average, reflecting the professional-grade equipment and facilities included. ‍ Budget-conscious photographers should consider suburban options farther from the CBD. Studios in Dandenong South and Hawthorn East can run as low as $45-$50 per hour, though the included equipment and amenities may be more limited. Hire a Professional Photographer Instead Renting a photography studio is the right call when you need a controlled environment with specific equipment, like a cyclorama, styled sets, or professional lighting rigs. For shoots where the location is more flexible, hiring a professional photographer who brings their own equipment and expertise can be a convenient alternative. ‍ Snappr connects you with experienced local photographers across Melbourne who handle the entire process, from booking to delivery of the edited photos. Whether you need headshots, product photography, event coverage, or corporate portraits, you can book a Melbourne photographer in as little as 12 hours. ‍ Snappr's photographers know Melbourne's best shooting locations and can recommend the right setting for your project, whether that's an indoor space, an office, or an outdoor location with natural lighting. Pricing starts at $59, with edited photos delivered within days. For businesses with ongoing photography needs, Snappr also offers managed photography services at scale. ‍ If your priority is professional results without managing the studio logistics yourself, it's an option worth exploring. Browse Melbourne photographers on Snappr → Frequently Asked Questions How Much Does It Cost to Rent a Photography Studio in Melbourne? Photography studio rental rates in Melbourne average $120 per hour. Prices range from about $45 per hour for basic suburban spaces to over $200 per hour for premium CBD studios. Most studios offer discounted rates for half-day (4 hours) and full-day (8 hours) bookings, which brings the effective hourly rate down. What Equipment Is Typically Included in a Melbourne Studio Hire? Most Melbourne photography studios include basic lighting equipment, backdrops, and grip gear in the hire price. Some also include advanced LED panels, strobes with modifiers, reflectors, and product tables. What's "included" varies significantly between studios, so check before booking. Do I Need to Bring My Own Camera and Lighting? You'll almost always need to bring your own camera body, lenses, and memory cards. Most studios provide lighting equipment, but the quality and range differ. Studios like SUNSTUDIOS Melbourne have on-site equipment hire departments where you can rent camera gear and additional lighting on the day. What Is a Cyclorama, and Do I Need One? A cyclorama (or "cyc") is a curved, seamless wall that eliminates corners and edges from your background. It's essential for clean product photography, fashion lookbooks, and any shoot requiring a solid-color or infinity backdrop. If you're shooting lifestyle or environmental portraits, you likely don't need one. Can I Hire a Melbourne Photography Studio for Video Production? Yes. Many studios on this list accommodate both photography and video production. Lithium Studios and XO Studios are particularly well-suited for film work, with high ceilings, sound considerations, and lighting rigs designed for continuous use. How Far in Advance Should I Book a Melbourne Photography Studio? Popular studios in South Melbourne and Fitzroy can book out one to two weeks ahead, especially on weekdays. Weekend availability tends to be more open at some locations, while self-access studios like Bohemia Bay are available year-round with flexible scheduling. Booking at least one week in advance is generally recommended.

title: Environmental Stewardship Guides Every Stage of Exploration
summary: Environmental stewardship means building environmental protections into the way exploration is planned, conducted, and reviewed.For offshore mineral exploration, safeguards begin before vessels enter the water. body_text: Environmental stewardship means building environmental protections into the way exploration is planned, conducted, and reviewed. For offshore mineral exploration, safeguards begin before vessels enter the water. Project teams review environmental data, identify sensitive areas, assess potential risks, and design measures to reduce disturbance. These measures can include defined operating areas, vessel operating procedures, environmental monitoring, reporting requirements, and activity-specific controls. Environmental protection continues throughout exploration. Environmental conditions are evaluated before field activities begin, monitored during operations, and reviewed afterward to confirm safeguards are working as intended. When new information becomes available, operators can adapt their approach, using scientific evidence to strengthen environmental protections and improve future operations. Regulatory oversight is also an important part of responsible exploration. In the United States, offshore marine mineral activities are subject to federal environmental review, scientific studies, and permitting requirements. In the Cook Islands, seabed mineral activities are governed by a dedicated regulatory framework that includes environmental assessment, monitoring, compliance, and enforcement. Good environmental stewardship means identifying potential impacts early, reducing them where possible, monitoring environmental conditions throughout operations, and being transparent about what is learned. For Odyssey, responsible exploration means gathering the scientific information needed to support informed decisions while protecting the marine environment throughout every stage of the exploration process.

title: eBay Completes Acquisition of Depop
summary: Today eBay announced it has completed its acquisition of Depop, a leading consumer to consumer fashion marketplace with a highly-engaged Gen Z and Millennial customer base.
body_text: SAN JOSE, Calif., July 30, 2026 – eBay Inc. (Nasdaq: EBAY), a global commerce leader that connects millions of buyers and sellers around the world, today announced that it has completed its acquisition of Depop, a leading consumer to consumer (C2C) fashion marketplace with a highly-engaged Gen Z and Millennial customer base. The acquisition builds on eBay’s continued momentum in fashion, a more than $10 billion annual GMV category for the company. With millions of users buying and selling fashion items, Depop has built one of the most vibrant and fastest-growing communities in fashion resale and cultivated a distinct, community-driven platform rooted in discovery, creativity, and peer-to-peer connection. Its highly engaged customer base and accessibly priced fashion inventory make Depop a natural complement to eBay’s leading proposition in C2C commerce. eBay intends to support Depop’s continued growth while preserving the elements that make the marketplace unique to accelerate the future of circular fashion. “As a global leader in C2C and recommerce, eBay’s acquisition of Depop further strengthens our C2C value proposition. This combines two distinct customer experiences and expands our reach with the next generation of buyers and sellers,” said Jamie Iannone, Chief Executive Officer of eBay. “Our goal is to preserve Depop’s strong brand, community, and product experience, while helping the team accelerate the roadmap that is already underway and explore synergies with eBay in areas that can supercharge our combined growth potential.” “Joining eBay, a company with a longstanding record of driving innovation in recommerce globally, is an exciting new chapter for Depop and our community,” said Peter Semple, Chief Executive Officer of Depop. “We’ve built a marketplace centered on creativity, self-expression, and connection, and we’re just getting started. Depop is a natural fit with eBay and together we can accelerate our growth while continuing to deliver the unique experience our users value.” As part of eBay, Depop will operate as a complementary business, retaining its distinct brand, platform, customer experience, and culture. By combining Depop’s category leadership with eBay’s global scale and capabilities — including shipping, personalization, compliance, and trusted services — we will enhance the buyer and seller experience and accelerate growth. About eBay eBay Inc. (Nasdaq: EBAY) is a global commerce leader that connects people and builds communities to create economic opportunity for all. Our technology empowers millions of buyers and sellers in more than 190 markets around the world, providing everyone the opportunity to grow and thrive. Founded in 1995 in San Jose, California, eBay is one of the world's largest and most vibrant marketplaces for discovering great value and unique selection. In 2025, eBay enabled nearly $80 billion of gross merchandise volume. For more information about the company and its global portfolio of online brands, visit www.ebayinc.com . About Depop Depop is the community-powered circular fashion marketplace where people can buy, sell and discover desirable, affordable secondhand fashion. Together with its global community of millions of users, Depop is on a mission to make fashion circular - encouraging more people to choose secondhand and extend the lives of their clothes, redefining fashion consumption. Founded in 2011, Depop’s diverse community has helped move resale into the mainstream, where buying secondhand is no longer an alternative, but how people of different ages now engage with fashion. title: Big Wave Riders | YETI Australia
summary: A calm mob of good-looking Brahman cattle is walking out across strong, grassy country in the NT’s Victoria River District.
body_text: A calm mob of good-looking Brahman cattle is walking out across strong, grassy country in the NT’s Victoria River District. Riders move along around the mob, keeping things in order as they head towards Wave Hill station’s Chungamidgee yards. Among those on the trail, talking quietly and taking it all in is a relaxed and happy Callum MacLachlan, who with a group of like-minded investors took on Wave Hill in 2021, becoming only the fourth owner of the iconic station in its 142 year history. “It’s an absolute highlight for me – spending time with the crew, on horseback, with the cattle out in front of us,” he says. At the heart of Wave Hill’s 1.25 million hectares are the people living and working there under the MacLachlan Pastoral Group banner. They are undertaking a program of major infrastructure development informed by their knowledge of effective and sustainable land management and an appreciation for the property’s history, potential and future. This extends beyond the pastoral sector to recognise the significance of the 1966 ‘Wave Hill Walk Off’ of Gurindji stockmen protesting wages and conditions, and the role the industry plays in the environmental, cultural and economic life of Australia. “There’s 3 million acres of country here, so it’s got economy of scale, which we can develop and which should equate to it being a fantastic business in the fullness of time,” Callum says.

title: Zapier vs. Tray comparison: Which is best for enterprise automation? [2026]
summary: You can use either platform for enterprise automation—but Tray is built for technical teams tackling complex problems, while Zapier lets anyone in your organization create the solutions they need.
body_text: It's easy to let edge cases influence your decision-making—thinking you need the most technical tool for the few times your developers will want to code their way out of a tough problem. And with enterprise software, it's tempting to assume you have to choose between power and ease of use. But that's not always true. The best automation platforms deliver both, scaling to meet complex enterprise needs while remaining intuitive enough for anyone to start building right away. You can use either Zapier or Tray for enterprise automation, but while Tray is built for technical teams, Zapier lets anyone in your organization create the automation and AI solutions they need. That's the gist, but let's look a little more at how Zapier and Tray compare in the ways that matter most for enterprise teams. Table of contents: Zapier vs. Tray at a glance Tray is for technical users; Zapier speeds up adoption by empowering everyone Zapier is faster and easier to deploy Zapier provides a comprehensive AI orchestration platform Zapier connects with 12x more apps than Tray Zapier is far more cost-effective Tray vs. Zapier: Which is best for your business? Zapier vs. Tray FAQ Zapier vs. Tray at a glance Both Zapier and Tray let you build powerful, complex automations and AI agents. The main difference is that Zapier is an accessible, no-code platform designed to empower everyone in your organization. And while Tray is expanding to cater to "business technologists," it still offers a more developer-centric automation approach. Here's a quick summary, but keep reading for a deeper comparison. Zapier Tray Ease of use Anyone can create automations with Zapier's no-code platform and AI copilot Built mostly for developers and technical users Implementation time Minutes to hours Days to weeks Pricing Transparent; starts at $19.99/month, with custom pricing available for enterprises Custom Integrations 9,000+ apps; connections are automatically maintained 700+ connectors; users must maintain connectors manually Enterprise security SOC 2 Type II, GDPR, SSO, audit logs SOC 2 Type II, GDPR, SSO, audit logs, HIPAA w/ PHI, data residency options AI capabilities Zapier Copilot lets anyone build automations, agents, process maps, databases, and forms; connects to 500+ AI apps; take actions from AI tools with Zapier MCP Tray offers an agent builder, pre-built agents, pre-built AI connectors, and vector tables for AI data Tray is geared toward technical users; Zapier speeds up adoption by empowering everyone to build safely Tray is geared toward technical users in large organizations. It's starting to add features that allow other teams to build alongside developers, but Tray still requires navigating complex options—including booleans, query strings, batch sizes, and dependencies—that make it inaccessible to non-technical teams. Image source: Tray Adding this level of complexity might be worth it in some circumstances. For example, Tray supports multi-level nested loops and offers lots of options for passing data between workflows. You can accomplish something similar with Sub-Zap workflows , Looping by Zapier , and Storage by Zapier , but for especially technical enterprise use cases, Tray offers greater precision for developers. But just because Tray can handle complex edge cases doesn't mean it's the best choice for your entire organization. By choosing a developer-focused automation tool, you confine all the energy, enthusiasm, and ideas around automation and AI to a small set of technical tinkerers in your IT department. Backlogs are an inevitable outcome as other departments come to rely on your developers to create and adjust workflows. Zapier is different. Non-technical teams can easily create and manage their own workflows, creating a bottom-up approach to automation and AI that accelerates adoption. For example, your marketing team can use Zapier Copilot to create automations by using natural language to describe what they want, like " Convert form sign-ups into personalized email sequences ." After asking a few questions to clarify the integrations and processes needed, Copilot designs a workflow and suggests next steps. With Zapier opening the door to automation self-service across your organization, IT teams can focus on the 20% of requests that require custom development instead of fielding basic support requests. Tray launched Agent Gateway for MCP in 2026, letting IT publish workflows and connector operations as governed MCP tools with RBAC, audit logging, and versioning. But getting there runs through Tray's signature gatekeeping, where a workspace admin has to request access, configure the server, define each tool's authentication, and add users to an allowlist before anyone can connect an AI client. It's MCP built for IT to administer centrally, not for a marketing team to use on their own. Zapier MCP skips that build-out. Install it once, and Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, or any MCP-compatible AI can act across Zapier's 9,000+ app integrations right away. Of course, that kind of democratization only works if it's safe. Every connection in Zapier is OAuth-managed, so credentials are never exposed to the person building the workflow or to any AI model in the loop. And IT can see exactly what's connected across the organization and revoke it in one place. Opening automation up to everyone doesn't mean losing track of who can touch what. Zapier is faster and easier to deploy Zapier Copilot is often the quickest way for non-technical users to get results, but the rest of Zapier's product stack is designed for speed, too. Take Zapier's Typeform to Google Sheets template , for example. Just connect the apps, confirm the form you want to use, and Zapier automatically pulls your most recent Typeform submissions to streamline the rest of the setup process. Once you've created a Google Sheet with appropriate column headings, just map your Typeform responses to the appropriate column in Google Sheets. And of course, if you want to create any variations on this template, you can just ask Zapier Copilot to create one for you. This ease of use on Zapier extends to even the most complex automations you might build. Tray has an equivalent Add Typeform survey responses to Google Sheets template, but it's not nearly as straightforward. You need to create a Typeform survey and Google Sheet that precisely map to the hardcoded values in Tray's static template. (For example, your Typeform survey must specifically include the question " What industry does your organization belong to? "). Once you've used Tray's static template to verify that all your connections, authentications, and triggers work properly, you need to adjust your project configuration to "dynamic workflow," delete all the content in your Google Sheet, and submit new questions and responses via Typeform. Image source: Tray Tray offers about 250 automation templates, but most are at least as complex to implement as the Typeform example—and they're almost entirely aimed at developers designing technical workflows. Some of Tray's newest features, like its Agent Builder, are more geared toward quick deployment. You can launch relatively quickly using Tray's pre-built agents and no-code building tools. But it still requires navigating far more configuration options than Zapier before publishing, which limits it to developers and extends deployment timelines. Image source: Tray Zapier provides a comprehensive AI orchestration platform Zapier started as an automation tool, but it now offers a much broader suite of capabilities including: AI agents you can build directly inside your workflows with AI by Zapier MCP for securely connecting to 9,000+ apps straight from your favorite AI tools Tables for storing and managing structured data Forms for building custom and shareable forms Canvas for visually mapping your business processes Combining these features into holistic workflows is what makes Zapier so powerful. Even better, you can use Zapier Copilot to create custom multi-product workflows that automatically access any Zapier products you need. In the example below—a customer survey form that stores responses and sends email notifications—Copilot identified that three tools were needed: Forms to create a customer-facing form Table to store and organize responses Zap workflows and Email by Zapier to send outbound email notifications Copilot then created a Canvas to orchestrate actions between the different products. With Tray, this process is far less integrated. Since Tray doesn't offer integrated forms or spreadsheets, you'd have to design a manual automation connecting multiple third-party services to collect and store your data, then use Tray's Send Email connector to send a notification.
